about: HELL palette mode ('Lava', candidate C of the owner's mock-ups): each 9-bit PC Engine colour (GGG RRR BBB) is sorted into a family by its HSV hue, saturation and value (channels 0-7 scaled to 0-1, hue in degrees) and re-coloured from that family's ramp. Grey or white (saturation below sat_low): 'ash' if value >= ash_v, else 'grey'. Otherwise 'blue' if blue_hue[0] <= hue <= blue_hue[1], 'green' if green_hue[0] <= hue < green_hue[1], else 'warm'. Ramps are [position, R, G, B] points (channels 0-7) interpolated linearly at: blue = value * lava_mix[0] + luma * lava_mix[1], green = luma * green_luma_scale, grey = value, ash = (value - ash_v) / (1 - ash_v); luma = R * luma[0] + G * luma[1] + B * luma[2] (0-1). Warm colours keep their hue when it is <= warm_keep_hue[0] or >= warm_keep_hue[1], else take warm_other_hue; hues from warm_magenta[0] up to warm_magenta[1] become warm_magenta[1]; saturation is multiplied by warm_s and value by warm_v. Colour 0 (black) stays black. Results round to 3 bits a channel. The mode recolours background palettes 0-14 (VCE entries 0-239) only; the HUD palette and the sprite palettes keep their colours. scripts/palette_tables.py turns this file into the 512-entry table at build time.
